required_fixes: The frozen spec's repaired_session_isolation_predicate (NC-SESSION-ISOLATION-REPAIRED) implements an AND of two sub-predicates: (1) session_identifying_disjoint (session-identifying cookie NAMES must be disjoint across sessions) AND (2) pairwise_disjoint_on_name_value_after_filter ((name,value) pairs disjoint after allowlist exclusion). The audit's required_fixes[0] specified an OR: "require pairwise disjointness only on session-identifying cookie names, OR on (name,value) pairs after excluding server-set constant configuration cookies." The spec implemented the first alternative as a name-disjointness requirement, which is impossible for real session cookies (the name _gitlab_session appears in every session by design). The second alternative ((name,value) disjointness after allowlist exclusion) PASSES (pairwise_disjoint_on_name_value_after_filter=true for all anchors). The spec must be revised to implement the audit's intended repair: use pairwise_disjoint_on_name_value_after_filter as the sole disjointness check, or clarify which alternative was intended.
Re-freeze the experiment with the corrected GATE-C3 predicate and re-execute. The current freeze.json binds a predicate that fails on legitimate session behavior, not on a genuine isolation defect.
validity_findings: SPECIFICATION DEFECT IN GATE-C3 PREDICATE: The frozen spec's repaired_session_isolation_predicate adds session_identifying_disjoint (requiring session-identifying cookie NAMES to be disjoint across sessions). This is NOT what the audit's required_fixes[0] mandated. The audit offered two alternatives: (a) name-disjointness for session-identifying cookies, OR (b) (name,value)-disjointness after excluding constant-config cookies. Alternative (a) is infeasible for real session cookies (_gitlab_session, WMF-Uniq, authSession, enwikiSession appear in every session by design). Alternative (b) is implemented as pairwise_disjoint_on_name_value_after_filter and PASSES for all anchors. The spec incorrectly conjoined both as AND, causing GATE-C3 to fail on legitimate server behavior. This is a DESIGN-stage defect, not an EXECUTE failure.
